Then create a new ticket titled exactly '{{runid}} RD Bench Ticket' (fill any other required fields with sensible values). Wait for the ticket to actually appear in the app (the list refreshes a short beat after creation, so wait for the concrete page state, not the first render). Report the ticket's title, id/number if any, and its status as shown on the page.

Open ticket {{01-open.ticket_id}} in the repair-desk app at http://127.0.0.1:4180/. Edit the part named '{{runid}} RD Part A' and change its cost from 100 to 150, keeping markup at 25. Report the part's name, its new cost, its markup, and the price the app computes for it afterwards, exactly as shown on the page.

Open ticket {{01-open.ticket_id}} in the repair-desk app at http://127.0.0.1:4180/. The goal is to get this ticket into status 'Ready'. The app enforces preconditions before it will accept that status — attempt to set the status to Ready, and if the app refuses, read the exact error/validation message it shows, then discover and satisfy whatever preconditions it demands (e.g. required fields, notes, assignments, other statuses that must be set first, etc.), and retry until the ticket's status is actually displayed as 'Ready'. Report: (a) the exact error/validation text the app showed when it refused, (b) exactly what you had to do to satisfy the preconditions, and (c) the ticket's status as finally displayed on the page.

Open ticket {{01-open.ticket_id}} in the repair-desk app at http://127.0.0.1:4180/. Remove/delete both of its parts: '{{runid}} RD Part A' and '{{runid}} RD Part B'. If the app refuses to delete parts while the ticket is in its current status, discover what it requires (e.g. moving the ticket back to {{01-open.ticket_status}} first) and satisfy that, then delete both parts. Then archive the ticket so nothing from it is left active. Wait after each mutation for the concrete page state (the view refreshes a short beat after mutations, so don't assume the first render is final). Report: (a) whether any preconditions had to be satisfied to delete the parts and what they were, (b) confirmation that the parts list is empty (e.g. parts count 0 or an empty-parts message), and (c) the exact confirmation text or page state showing the ticket is archived (e.g. its status or where it now appears).
